proofs.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{ass:disturbance-positive-definiteness}\),
\(\Gamma_j[a,a]>0\) for every \(j\).  By
\(\texttt{ass:component-aligned-disturbances}\), the within-view disturbance
covariance is therefore the positive-definite diagonal matrix
\(\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(\Gamma_j[a,a])\).  Assumption
\(\texttt{ass:shared-topological-order}\) makes
\(L^{0,(a)}=I_p-B^{0,(a)}\) invertible, and
\(\texttt{ass:linear-structural-equations}\) gives
\[
 \Sigma^{aa}=(L^{0,(a)})^{-1}
 \operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(\Gamma_j[a,a])
 (L^{0,(a)})^{-\mathsf T}\succ0.
\]
Thus every principal matrix \(\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\) is positive definite and the
inverse below exists.
By \(\texttt{def:modified-cholesky}\), if the predecessor set of \(r\) is
\(A\), the nonzero part of its row is the unique solution \(c\) of the normal
equations
\[
 c\,\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]=\Sigma^{aa}[r,A].
\]
Right multiplication by the inverse gives
\[
 c=\Sigma^{aa}[r,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}.
\]
By \(\texttt{def:immutable-original-row}\), this is exactly
\(\beta^{(a)}(A,r)[A]\), and both definitions put zero in every column in
\(V\setminus A\).  Hence
\[
 B_\pi^{(a)}[r,\mathord\cdot]=\beta^{(a)}(A,r).
\]
Permuting the order in which the columns indexed by \(A\) are displayed
permutes the normal equations and their solution in the same way; restoring
the original column labels therefore leaves the displayed row unchanged.
Variables in the suffix do not occur in the normal equations and occupy
zero columns in both definitions.  This proves both invariance assertions.

Write \(L^{0,(a)}=I_p-B^{0,(a)}\), and let \(\Sigma_{\rm full}\) denote the
covariance of the full vector \((X^{(a)}:a\in M)\), including the conceptually
present nonedge blocks.  By \(\texttt{ass:shared-topological-order}\), every
\(L^{0,(a)}\) is unit triangular after the common permutation \(\pi_0\), hence
is invertible.  By \(\texttt{ass:component-aligned-disturbances}\), the full
disturbance covariance \(\Omega\) satisfies
\[
 \Omega[(a,i),(b,j)]={\bf1}\{i=j\}\,\Gamma_i[a,b].
\]
After grouping indices by \(i\), this matrix is
\(\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}(\Gamma_i)\).  Every block is positive definite
by \(\texttt{ass:disturbance-positive-definiteness}\), so \(\Omega\succ0\).
The structural equations in
\(\texttt{ass:linear-structural-equations}\) now give
\[
 \Sigma_{\rm full}
 =\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L^{0,(a)})^{-1}
   \Omega
   \operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L^{0,(a)})^{-\mathsf T}
 \succ0.
\]
Consequently every \(\Sigma^{aa}\) and every principal matrix
\(\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\) is positive definite.  The inverses in
\(\texttt{def:modified-cholesky}\),
\(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\), and
\(\texttt{def:q-root-score}\) therefore exist.  Moreover, each within-view
Schur complement \(C_A^{aa}\) is positive definite, so
\(C_A^{aa}[r,r]>0\).  This justifies every division below.

We first prove the path criterion.  Orthogonal projection onto the span of
\(X_A^{(a)}\), followed by projection onto the residual of \(X_r^{(a)}\), is
orthogonal projection onto the span of \(X_{A\cup\{r\}}^{(a)}\): both sides
are orthogonal to that span, and an orthogonal projection is unique because
its Gram matrix is positive definite.  Hence, for
\(t\in U_A\setminus\{r\}\),
\[
 Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)}
 =Z_{A,t}^{(b)}-
   \frac{C_A^{bb}[t,r]}{C_A^{bb}[r,r]}Z_{A,r}^{(b)}.
\]
Taking covariance with \(Z_{A,r}^{(a)}\) and using symmetry of
\(C_A^{bb}\) yields
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P\!\left(
 Z_{A,r}^{(a)},Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)}\right)
 =C_A^{ab}[r,t]-C_A^{ab}[r,r]
   \{C_A^{bb}[r,r]\}^{-1}C_A^{bb}[r,t]
 =q^{ab}(A,r,t).                                      \tag{1}
\]
This also proves from \(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\) that the
state after removing a set is a function of that set and the fixed covariance
blocks, rather than of the path used to reach it.

Fix a permutation whose next label after \(A\) is \(r\), and let
\(W=U_A\setminus\{r\}\) in the order supplied by the suffix.  Sequential
within-view regression of the variables in \(W\) gives an invertible unit
triangular matrix \(K^{(b)}\) such that the final innovation vector is
\[
 e_W^{(b)}=K^{(b)}Z_{A\cup\{r\},W}^{(b)},
 \qquad e_r^{(a)}=Z_{A,r}^{(a)}.
\]
Equation (1) therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_r^{(a)},e_W^{(b)})
 =\bigl(q^{ab}(A,r,t):t\in W\bigr)(K^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.       \tag{2}
\]
Since \(K^{(b)}\) is invertible, the left side of (2) is zero if and only if
all its displayed \(q^{ab}\)-scores are zero.  Reversing \(a,b\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_W^{(a)},e_r^{(b)})
 =K^{(a)}\bigl(q^{ba}(A,r,t):t\in W\bigr)^{\mathsf T},        \tag{3}
\]
so both orientations in \(\texttt{def:removed-set-compatibility-dag}\) are
necessary and sufficient for the row and column involving \(r\) to have no
off-diagonal entries.  Applying (2)--(3) successively along the permutation,
with the one-variable suffix as the base case, proves
\[
 \pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }\mathcal D_G
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0
 \text{ for every }\{a,b\}\in E.                            \tag{4}
\]
The same normal equations show that \(R_\pi^{aa}\) is diagonal for every
view: an earlier innovation is orthogonal to the span on which every later
variable is regressed.

It remains to verify, rather than assume, the completion part of
\(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\).  For an arbitrary \(\pi\), let
\[
 L_\pi=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L_\pi^{(a)}),
 \qquad S_\pi=L_\pi\Sigma_{\rm full}L_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Each \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is unit triangular in order \(\pi\), so it is invertible,
and the already proved \(\Sigma_{\rm full}\succ0\) gives \(S_\pi\succ0\).
For \(j\in V\), let \(H_{\pi,j}\) be the principal submatrix of \(S_\pi\)
on the indices \(\{(a,j):a\in M\}\).  Principal submatrices of a positive
definite matrix are positive definite, because for nonzero \(u\in\mathbb R^m\)
its zero extension \(\widetilde u\) satisfies
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}H_{\pi,j}u
 =\widetilde u^{\mathsf T}S_\pi\widetilde u>0.
\]
For a diagonal view block or an observed edge, the corresponding block of
\(S_\pi\) is exactly
\(L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}=R_\pi^{ab}\).
Thus \(H_{\pi,j}\) agrees with every specified entry of \(Q_{\pi,j}\) and is
a positive-definite completion.  This conclusion holds for every candidate
order and every arbitrary view graph on a maintained-model input.  Combining
it with (4) and \(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\) proves
\[
 \pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }\mathcal D_G
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G).    \tag{5}
\]

Finally suppose (equivalently by (5)) that these conditions hold.  For each
\(j\), choose the just-constructed completion
\(\Gamma_j^\pi=H_{\pi,j}\), and take mutually independent centered Gaussian
vectors \((\eta_j^{(a)}:a\in M)\) with covariances \(\Gamma_j^\pi\).  Put
\(\eta^{(a)}=(\eta_j^{(a)}:j\in V)\) and define
\[
 \widetilde X^{(a)}=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\eta^{(a)}.
\]
Then the coefficient matrices are exactly \(B_\pi^{(a)}\), share order
\(\pi\), and satisfy
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_i^{(a)},\eta_j^{(b)})=0
 \quad(i\ne j),
 \qquad \operatorname{Cov}((\eta_j^{(a)})_{a\in M})
 =\Gamma_j^\pi\succ0.
\]
Thus the assembled law satisfies all five member properties in
\(\texttt{def:component-aligned-limvam-class}\); Gaussianity makes the
independently assembled coordinate stacks a joint centered Gaussian vector.
On diagonal blocks and edges, (4) and the within-view diagonality give
\(\operatorname{Cov}(\eta^{(a)},\eta^{(b)})=R_\pi^{ab}\), whence
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)},\widetilde X^{(b)})
 =(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}R_\pi^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{-\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma^{ab}.
\]
The constructed completion therefore has the observed law
\(\mathcal O_G\) and coefficient tuple \(T_\pi\), as claimed.

Because \(\rho\) and \(\rho'\) end at a live vertex, source-to-sink pruning
in \(\texttt{def:removed-set-compatibility-dag}\) guarantees at least one
path from \(A\) to \(V\).  A suffix is precisely such a path, so its legality
depends only on its initial subset \(A\), not on either path used to reach
\(A\).

Write a legal suffix as \((r_1,\ldots,r_{p-|A|})\) and set
\(A_0=A\), \(A_s=A_{s-1}\cup\{r_s\}\).  By
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), the rows contributed by this suffix
are, in their immutable original labels,
\[
 \beta(A_0,r_1),\ \beta(A_1,r_2),\ \ldots,\
 \beta(A_{p-|A|-1},r_{p-|A|}).                              \tag{6}
\]
Every term in (6) depends only on the fixed input and the displayed subset,
so the same suffix appends exactly the same rows to \(F(\rho)\) and
\(F(\rho')\).  It follows immediately that
\[
 F(\rho)=F(\rho')
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Comp}(\rho)=\operatorname{Comp}(\rho').     \tag{7}
\]

Conversely, suppose the completion sets are equal.  They are nonempty by
liveness, so choose \(T\) in their common value.  No assigned row is ever
overwritten in \(\texttt{def:live-fragment-completions}\); applying
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\) to an inducing full path shows that
the projection of \(T\) onto original row labels in \(A\) is both
\(F(\rho)\) and \(F(\rho')\).  Hence these fragments are equal.  The same
argument needs only one common tuple, and therefore proves the stronger
implication
\[
 \operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\cap\operatorname{Comp}(\rho')\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(\rho)=F(\rho').                \tag{8}
\]
Taking the contrapositive of (8) proves the asserted disjointness.  Together,
(7)--(8) prove the equivalence, disjointness, and suffix-independence claims.

For a subset \(A\), let \(\mathcal P_A\) be the live prefixes ending at
\(A\).  We first prove by induction on \(|A|\) the exact dictionary invariant
\[
 H_A=\{F(\rho):\rho\in\mathcal P_A\},                       \tag{9}
\]
with the right side empty for a nonlive subset.  At \(A=\varnothing\), (9)
is the initialization in \(\texttt{def:fragment-hashcons-enumerator}\).
Every nonempty live prefix has a last transition
\(A\setminus\{r\}\to A\); by the induction hypothesis its parent fragment
is present, and the algorithm appends precisely \(\beta(A\setminus\{r\},r)\),
so its fragment is inserted.  Conversely, every attempted insertion follows
a live edge from a represented live prefix and hence represents a member of
\(\mathcal P_A\).  Exact trie equality removes only equal fragments.  This
proves (9).

Fix \(F\in H_A\) and choose a representing \(\rho\) using (9).  Liveness
gives a suffix from \(A\) to \(V\), so
\(\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\ne\varnothing\).  By
\(\texttt{lem:live-fragment-right-congruence}\), this completion set depends
only on \(F\), and distinct \(F\)'s give disjoint nonempty completion sets.
By \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), every source-to-sink path is
an order in \(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\); hence each of those sets is a subset of
\(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\).  Moreover, the immutable-row lemma shows for
every \(T\in\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\) that
\[
 T\big|_{\text{rows }A}=F.                                  \tag{10}
\]
Thus the completion sets provide pairwise disjoint nonempty charges from
the members of \(H_A\) into the \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\) outputs, and
\[
 |H_A|\le N_{\mathrm{out}}.                                 \tag{11}
\]
Summing (11) over the \(2^p\) subsets gives
\[
 \sum_{A\subseteq V}|H_A|\le 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}.           \tag{12}
\]
Finally a subset vertex has at most \(p-|A|\le p\) outgoing transitions.
Each retained fragment is processed once, so (12) yields
\[
 \#\{\text{attempted fragment transitions}\}
 \le\sum_{A\subseteq V}p|H_A|
 \le p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}.
\]
This proves every claimed projection and counting assertion.

The dictionary invariant (9), already proved in
\(\texttt{lem:projection-output-bound}\), says that \(H_V\) is exactly the
set of full fragments of source-to-sink paths.  At \(V\) no row is
unassigned.  By \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), such a fragment is
the tuple \(T_\pi\) of its path; by
\(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), those paths are exactly the
orders in \(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\).  Therefore
\[
 H_V=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\}
 =\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G).                                   \tag{13}
\]
An integer-trie terminal is created only on its first insertion, and row
identifiers are equal exactly when all their exact-real coordinates are
equal.  Thus (13) is emitted with neither omissions nor numerical duplicates.

We now count operations in the declared model \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ER}}\).
There are \(2^p\) subset vertices and at most \(p2^{p-1}\) subset edges.
For each \(A\), all within-view principal solves and all edgewise covariance
states can be computed directly from the input by
\[
 D_A^{(a)}=\Sigma^{aa}[U_A,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1},
\]
\[
 C_A^{ab}=\Sigma^{ab}[U_A,U_A]
 -D_A^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}[A,U_A]
 -\Sigma^{ab}[U_A,A](D_A^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}
 +D_A^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}[A,A](D_A^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.          \tag{14}
\]
Dense elimination and multiplication in (14), including all immutable rows,
cost
\[
 O\!\left((m+|E|)p^3 2^p\right)
\]
field operations.  All \(q\)-tests add
\(O(|E|p^2 2^p)\) exact comparisons and operations, and forward/backward
pruning adds \(O(p2^p)\); both are absorbed by the preceding bound because
\(p,m\ge2\).

For a fixed original row label \(r\), at most \(2^{p-1}\) live edges carry
that label.  Lexicographic comparison of two viewwise rows uses at most
\(mp\) ordered exact-real comparisons, and comparison sorting uses
\(O(K_r\log(K_r+1))\) row comparisons.  Since
\(\log_2(K_r+1)=O(p)\), summing over \(r\) gives
\[
 O\!\left(mp\sum_{r\in V}K_r\log(K_r+1)\right)
 =O(mp^3 2^p),                                               \tag{15}
\]
which is again absorbed in the preprocessing term.  Sorting adjacent equal
rows into one identifier proves that equality of identifiers is equivalent
to numerical row equality; no real-valued hash is used.

Each identifier needs \(O(p)\) binary digits because
\(K_r+1\le2^{p-1}+1\).  A fragment has \(p\) slots, so a deterministic binary
trie lookup or insertion uses \(O(p^2)\) bit/pointer operations.  By
\(\texttt{lem:projection-output-bound}\), at most
\(p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\) transitions are attempted.  Fragment propagation
therefore costs
\[
 O(p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}).                                \tag{16}
\]
Decoding the \(m\) matrices of each of the \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\) outputs costs
\(O(mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}})\).  Adding (14)--(16) proves the explicit time bound
\[
 O\!\left((m+|E|)p^3 2^p+p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}
                 +mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}}\right).              \tag{17}
\]

For completeness, the covariance states use
\(O((m+|E|)p^2 2^p)\) real cells, the interned rows use
\(O(mp^2 2^p)\) cells, and the tries use
\(O(p^2 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}})\) bits/pointers; decoded output uses
\(O(mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}})\) cells if retained rather than streamed.  These
time and space bounds are
\[
 O\!\left(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p
                 \max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\}\right).
\]
Every loop is over a subset state, a retained fragment, or an outgoing subset
edge.  No loop ranges over compatible permutations, which proves the final
algorithmic assertion.

Suppose \(B^{0,(a)}=0\) for every \(a\).  The structural equations give
\(X^{(a)}=\varepsilon^{(a)}\).  By
\(\texttt{ass:component-aligned-disturbances}\), for every view
\(\Sigma^{aa}\) is diagonal, and its diagonal entries are strictly positive
because each \(\Gamma_j\succ0\) by
\(\texttt{ass:disturbance-positive-definiteness}\).  Hence for every
\(A\subseteq V\), \(r\notin A\), and \(a\in M\),
\[
 \Sigma^{aa}[r,A]=0,
 \qquad
 \beta^{(a)}(A,r)=0.                                       \tag{18}
\]
The immutable-row lemma shows that every order, and in particular every
compatible order, therefore induces the same all-zero coefficient tuple.

If \(E=\varnothing\), the conjunction of \(q\)-conditions defining every
subset edge is empty, so \(\mathcal D_G\) is the full subset lattice and all
\(p!\) permutations are source-to-sink paths.  Equivalently, each
\(Q_{\pi,j}\) specifies only its positive diagonal and admits that diagonal
matrix as a positive-definite completion, so every order lies in
\(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\).  Thus (18) gives
\(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{0\}\) and \(N_{\mathrm{out}}=1\).
All subset vertices are live.  Starting from the one empty fragment, every
transition writes the same zero row, and exact duplicate insertion retains
one and only one fragment at each \(A\).  There are \(2^p\) subsets, so the
total number of retained fragments is exactly \(2^p\), as claimed.

theorem.statement:
Under the premises of
\(\texttt{thm:exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\), suppose every entry
of the rational input \(\mathcal O_G\) has binary encoding length at most
\(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\).  The fraction-free immutable-row implementation of
\(\operatorname{Enum}_G\) has deterministic total bit-operation time and
bit storage polynomial in \(p\), \(m\), \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\), \(2^p\),
\(N_{\mathrm{out}}\), and the total emitted encoding length.  Canonically
reduced determinant-ratio certificates decide equality of interned rows.
Thus no superpolynomial intermediate or certificate growth is forced in
this maintained-model rational regime.
theorem.proof_tex:
Let an input rational be written in lowest terms.  For any one principal
regression solve, multiply its augmented matrix by the product \(d\) of the
denominators of its at most \((p+1)^2\) entries.  Since each input numerator
and denominator has at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\) binary digits,
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(d)\le(p+1)^2L_{\mathrm{bits}},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{bits}(d x)=O(p^2L_{\mathrm{bits}})            \tag{19}
\]
for every scaled entry \(dx\).  Scaling the coefficient matrix and right-hand
side by the same nonzero \(d\) does not change the regression solution.
Maintained-model membership, as proved in
\(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), makes every principal covariance
matrix positive definite.  Hence its leading principal minors in any fixed
ordering of \(A\) are positive, so all pivots required by the no-pivot
fraction-free recurrence are nonzero.

By \(\texttt{lem:bareiss-minor-growth}\), every integer produced by that
recurrence is a signed minor of the scaled augmented matrix and every exact
division has zero remainder.  We now bound those minors directly.  If a
\(k\times k\) integer matrix has entries of magnitude less than \(2^h\), the
Leibniz formula gives
\[
 |\det K|
 \le\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_k}
       \prod_{i=1}^k|K_{i,\sigma(i)}|
 < k!\,2^{kh}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(\det K)
 \le kh+\lceil\log_2(k!)\rceil+1
 =O\!\left(p^3L_{\mathrm{bits}}+p\log p\right),             \tag{20}
\]
where (19) and \(k\le p+1\) were used.  The numerator and denominator of
each coordinate of \(\beta(A,r)\) are such bordered/principal minors.  Divide
them by their greatest common divisor and choose a positive denominator.
This produces a canonical rational pair of the bit length in (20), so two
row coordinates are equal if and only if their canonical pairs are equal.
The vector of these pairs, followed by the deterministic sorting identifier,
is the requested canonical row-equality certificate.

The definition of the projected residual state gives directly
\[
 C_A^{ab}=\Sigma^{ab}[U_A,U_A]
 -D_A^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}[A,U_A]
 -\Sigma^{ab}[U_A,A](D_A^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}
 +D_A^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}[A,A](D_A^{(b)})^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 D_A^{(a)}=\Sigma^{aa}[U_A,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}.
\]
After expanding these matrix products, one entry is a sum of at most
\(1+2p+p^2\) products of input rationals and regression coordinates.  The
scores \(q^{ab}(A,r,t)\) use two further products and one division by the
strictly positive rational \(C_A^{bb}[r,r]\).  Canonical rational addition,
multiplication, division, and greatest-common-divisor reduction therefore
keep the numerator and denominator lengths bounded by a polynomial in
\(p\) and \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\); for example, multiplying all denominators
term by term in the displayed expansions and using (20) gives the coarse
bound
\[
 O\!\left(p^5(L_{\mathrm{bits}}+\log p)\right)              \tag{21}
\]
bits per covariance-state or score entry.  Each state is computed directly
from the original input, so (21) is not iterated through the \(2^p\) states.

The exact-real proof counted a number of field operations and comparisons
polynomial in
\(p,m,2^p,N_{\mathrm{out}}\).  By (19)--(21), each is implemented by addition,
multiplication, exact division, comparison, or greatest common divisor on
integers of polynomial bit length.  The grade-school algorithms for the
first four operations use polynomially many bit operations.  Euclid's
algorithm does as well: after at most two remainder steps its positive second
operand is less than half its earlier value, so inputs of \(h\) bits require
at most \(2h+1\) divisions, each on at most \(h\)-bit integers.  Fragment keys
contain \(p\) identifiers of \(O(p)\)
bits and hence introduce no rational-expression growth.  Finally, writing
the decoded rational matrices costs exactly their emitted encoding length.
Multiplying the polynomial per-operation cost by the operation counts in
\(\texttt{thm:exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\), and adding that
output-writing cost, proves the asserted polynomial bit time.  The same
bit-length bounds times the stored-entry and trie-node counts prove the
storage assertion.  This answers the open-ended question affirmatively on
its stated maintained-model rational input class.
theorem.justification: The ordered exact-real guarantee lifts to a deterministic output-polynomial Turing-model guarantee because every rational covariance-state entry is a bounded-degree determinant rational computed directly from the input.
theorem.gap: Bareiss's integer-preserving elimination controls each solve, but the theorem additionally proves simultaneous polynomial height for all subset-indexed regression rows, root scores, canonical equality certificates, fragment keys, and emitted tuples.
theorem.consumer: Exact symbolic implementations may advertise polynomial bit complexity on rational maintained-model inputs, while retaining the note's exclusions for off-model completion and numerical floating-point stability.

added_lemmas.statement:
For an integer symmetric positive-definite coefficient matrix augmented by
integer right-hand sides, the Bareiss fraction-free elimination recurrences
without pivoting make only exact integer divisions, and every transformed
coefficient is a signed bordered minor of the augmented input matrix.

source.locator: Section I, equations (3)--(7), together with the one-step integer-preserving elimination developed in Section II

attestation.note: Checked against Bareiss (1968), Sections I--II; the stable DOI is supplied in place of a verbatim transcription.

proposed.statement: Let \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\), and suppose the predecessor set of \(r\) under \(\pi\) is exactly \(A\). Then the original-label row \(B_\pi^{(a)}[r,\cdot]\) equals \(\beta^{(a)}(A,r)\) for every \(a\in M\). Hence that row is invariant to the order within \(A\) and to every suffix after \(r\).
proposed.justification: The immutable row is the model-specific write-once label that replaces the failed completed-path quotient.
proposed.gap: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Appendix D.3, preserves the residual LiMVAM after removing a recovered root, but it does not express every orderwise structural row as a function of its original-label predecessor set for quotient enumeration.
proposed.consumer: A duplicate-free calibration solver can cache a row once and never replay the removal history that produced it.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen dependencies did not suffice to derive the nonsingularity needed by the regression inverse. Component alignment makes each within-view disturbance covariance diagonal positive definite, and the shared order makes the structural residualizer invertible, so these two existing assumptions must be declared in the proof spine.

proposed.statement: For every \(A\subseteq V\), each retained fragment in \(H_A\) is the projection onto rows indexed by \(A\) of at least one tuple in \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\), distinct fragments at \(A\) project to disjoint nonempty output subsets, and therefore \(|H_A|\le N_{\mathrm{out}}\), \(\sum_{A\subseteq V}|H_A|\le2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\), and the number of attempted fragment transitions is at most \(p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\).
proposed.justification: The projection charge converts a compact state representation into a total cost controlled by numerical outputs rather than compatible orders.
proposed.gap: WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, Theorem 4, gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration for graph-distinct outputs, and DeepHuKoutris2021ProjectedEnumeration, Theorem 7, gives output-dependent delay for projected star-query enumeration after linear preprocessing. Neither bounds numerical coefficient fragments in a causal removed-set DAG by the final tuple count.
proposed.consumer: Sparse or degenerate LiMVAM systems with many compatible orders but few coefficient tuples avoid factorial intermediate storage.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof must invoke path exactness to conclude that every live source-to-sink completion belongs to the compatible-order estimand; the frozen dependency list omitted that load-bearing edge.
